long_biography.plain_text:
Powered flight gave Russell Alexander Alger Jr. another place to test his judgement as an industrial investor. He backed the Wright brothers, helped form the Wright Company with Cornelius Vanderbilt III and August Belmont Jr., and later invested in Detroit's General Aeroplane Company. One of the Wrights' early aircraft became his own.

Physical risk appealed to him too. Alger rode, sailed, shot and played golf, earning a reputation as a fierce competitor. A riding accident in 1921 left him paralysed and brought active business life to an abrupt close. His lakeside Grosse Pointe home, The Moorings, outlasted that career: commissioned from architect Charles A. Platt, it later became a public cultural centre and memorial to local war service.
